title: Evaluation and Explainability of Unsupervised Scholarly Collaboration Recommendations
subcategory: scholarly recommendation with topic-based researcher profiles
task: Unsupervised content-based collaborator recommendation from titles and abstracts
problem: Collaboration recommenders based on lexical overlap may not generalise when shared publications are absent; explainability is also needed.
architecture: Compares TF-IDF profiles, topic-based researcher graphs (LDA and BERTopic with SciBERT encoder, plus 'clone' variants that split prolific researchers by local topic clusters; Jensen-Shannon similarity, Louvain communities), and SciBERT + Faiss retrieval; explanations via shared topics/word clouds or retrieved papers summarised by GPT-OSS-120B.
metrics: Hits@10 (historical co-authorship as proxy ground truth)
key_results: Full data: TF-IDF is best (MSU MRR 0.597 vs 0.430 for LDA).
50/50 holdout on MWC: Faiss MRR 0.272 and Clone-LDA 0.267 vs 0.207 for TF-IDF; BERTopic variants are weakest (e.g. MSU MRR 0.107).
strengths: Tests robustness when shared publication text is removed.

limitations.text: OpenAlex metadata may not fully represent researcher profiles.
Co-authorship is only a proxy for real collaboration potential; no human evaluation.

notes: Application study from the author-curated corpus.
